llm.summary: The skill is broadly a beauty booking assistant, but it has enough under-disclosed booking, data-sharing, and catalog-scope issues that users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: Appointment booking, price lookup, page opening, and recommendations mostly fit the BeautsGO booking purpose, but the provider catalog also includes airport transfer, telecom, styling/photoshoot, and BeautsGO storefront entries that can be surfaced through the same workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill documents direct appointment submission and browser opening, but booking submission happens after the user provides date/details without a separate final confirmation step, and the privacy section omits the third-party price-query endpoint.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Normal installation is described through package managers, but bundled helper scripts can bulk-copy the skill into all local Cowork session skill directories, delete prior copies, and restart an OpenClaw gateway if manually run.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access to BeautsGO booking/pages is purpose-aligned, but the separate beise.com price API and hardcoded authorization token are not fully covered by the privacy disclosure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The runtime does not show background persistence or credential-store access, but the bundled maintenance/install scripts have broad local mutation behavior outside the normal skill runtime.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with BeautsGO receiving appointment details such as preferred date and phone number, and with price search terms being sent to a separate beise.com API. Confirm the selected provider before submitting any booking, because the catalog includes some non-clinic services. Do not run the included local install/sync scripts unless you trust the publisher and intend to modify local agent skill directories or restart OpenClaw services.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Opening BeautsGO pages, chat pages, price pages, and giving recommendations are related to booking, but the scanner's concern is partly supported because the top-level privacy/purpose text does not fully disclose the separate price-query API and recommendation behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: The beise.com price lookup is expected for price queries, but the privacy section only names the BeautsGO appointment API, so this is a valid transparency gap.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Airport transfer entries in data/hospitals.json are not expected for a clinic and medical-aesthetic appointment catalog.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Telecom entries in the hospital catalog exceed the declared clinic-booking scope and could be routed through the same booking flow.
[SDI-1] unexpected: BeautsGO storefront/self listings blur neutral provider selection and platform commerce inside a provider catalog.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Hair, makeup, and photoshoot listings are broader than the dermatology/plastic-surgery framing and should be separated or clearly disclosed.
